content.title: About
content.content: Gordita with meat and beans is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a soft corn pocket filled with seasoned ground beef, boiled beans, cheese, and salsa. Served hot, it is often topped with sour cream or guacamole.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “gordita” means “little fat one” in Spanish, referring to its plump shape.
Originally cooked on an open flame, the tortilla develops a lightly charred edge.
The meat‑bean combination provides a complete amino‑acid profile, making the dish nutritionally balanced.
In the United States, gorditas are popular in fast‑food settings, but the authentic version remains homemade with fresh ingredients.
Variations include chicken, pork, vegetables, and vegetarian versions with tofu.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Ground beef and beans together deliver high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Beans are an excellent source of fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both meat and beans provide B6 and B12, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, zinc, and magnesium, nutrients vital for immunity, blood formation, and muscle function.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Corn tortilla and beans have a moderate glycemic index, helping maintain stable glucose levels.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn products, including the tortilla.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared salsa or added salt can increase sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of meat, cheese, and dough makes the dish calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Proper meat cooking
items.content: Ground beef must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gorditas are hand‑eaten; split them open and add sour cream, guacamole, fresh veggies, or a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or skillet to restore the crisp tortilla texture.
